Is anyone else genuinely surprised that backwards compat on Xbox One is proving to be a huge profit for both MS and the devs?

It seems like it's doing a lot of good on both fronts. I do sincerely wonder if it's actually emulation on the back-end or if Microsoft is manually porting each game over and hosting them in the store. When you play a backwards compatible game you always end up having to download the whole thing from Microsoft instead of installing it from disc. It would also explain why games go up a handful at a time instead of many at once.

There may be a few things required by MS, but other than those few things it's gotta be emulation... The online functionality would break if they were ported over completely by hand. You'll notice some games work better than others too.

That makes sense. I wonder how much of the code is original and how much is new code being applied as an update to each title. It could be that it would run perfectly fine from the disc, or with disc+update, but Microsoft has some other reason for making each game a download.
It may just simply be that they want things to be controlled digitally. Who knows. Maybe we'll find out down the line.
That does sound like a Microsoft-y reason, so I wouldn't be surprised if you're right. I appreciate the insights, Codewow; you always have a good perspective to add.

They are not porting games, they are recreating the xbox 360 hardware as software. They mentioned once that releasing new games is slow because they have to get developer approval, and then each game has to be custom packaged with the emulator wrapper.

It was stupid to ever remove it. The PS3 kind of made sense, it was expensive to keep the PS2 emotion chip in the PS3, but since then emulation has become much easier and other than laziness, there really isn't a good reason not to include backwards compatibility.
They didn't "remove" it. They changed the architecture from powerpc to standard x86. This made running those games impossible without emulation.

Surprised? No. The Xbox 360 had a looong life with a lot of good titles- that people are going to want to play them again after they've traded their away their original copies to Gamestop is no surprise- then, too, there are players who weren't alive when the 360 originally released- so while I'm glad that they've adopted backwards compatibility, since it's a very pro-consumer move, it was unsurprising in that it was a smart move.

Also, they're not charging people extra to play stuff they already own. Take note, Nintendo.
